==English== {{swp}} ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*steh₂-}} From {{inh|en|enm|estat}}, from {{der|en|xno|estat}} and {{der|en|fro|estat}} (French: {{m|fr|état}}), from {{der|en|la|status}}. {{doublet|en|state|status}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|ĭ-stāt|a=RP,GA}}, {{IPA|en|/ɪˈsteɪt/}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-estate.ogg|a=US}} ** {{rhymes|en|eɪt|s=2}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun}} # The collective property and liabilities of someone, especially a deceased person. {{defdate|from 19th c.}} # {{lb|en|now|_|rare|archaic}} [[state|State]]; [[condition]]. {{defdate|from 13th c.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Twelfth Night|act=V|scene=i|page=275|passage=But when I came to mans '''eſtate''',
With hey ho, [the winde and the raine],
Gainſt Knaues and Theeues men ſhut their gate.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1643|author=w:John Milton|title=Doctrine and Discipline of Divorce |passage=To remove therfore if it be possible, this great and sad oppression which through the strictnes of a literall interpreting hath invaded and disturb’d the dearest and most peaceable '''estate''' of houshold society, to the over-burdening, if not the over-whelming of many Christians better worth then to be so deserted of the Churches considerate care, this position shall be laid down; first proving, then answering what may be objected either from Scripture or light of reason.}} # {{lb|en|archaic}} [[status|Status]], [[rank]]. {{defdate|from 13th c.}} #* {{RQ:Taylor Holy Living|passage=God hath imprinted his authority in several parts, upon several '''estates''' of men.}} # {{lb|en|archaic}} The condition of one's [[fortune]]s; [[prosperity]], [[possession]]s. {{defdate|from 14th c.}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Romans|12|16|passage=Mind not high things, but condescend to men of low '''estate'''.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} A "person of estate"; a [[nobleman]] or [[noblewoman]]. {{defdate|14th|17th c.}} #* {{RQ:Mlry MrtDrthr|18.11|2|XVI|xj|passage=And anone came oute of a chamber to hym the fayrest lady that euer he sawe & more rycher bysene than euer he sawe Quene Gueneuer or ony other '''estat''' Lo sayd they syre Bors here is the lady vnto whome we owe alle oure seruyse / and I trowe she be the rychest lady and the fayrest of alle the world}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Mark|6|21|passage=Herod on his birthday made a supper to his lords, high captains, and chief '''estates''' of Galilee.}} # {{lb|en|historical}} A major social class or order of persons regarded collectively as part of the body politic of the country and formerly possessing distinct political rights ({{w|Estates of the realm}}). {{defdate|from 14th c.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1992|author=w:Hilary Mantel|title=w:A Place of Greater Safety|publisher=Harper Perennial|year_published=2007|page=115 |passage=I am afraid that some of the nobles who are campaigning for it simply want to use the '''Estates''' to cut down the King's power and increase their own.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2011|author=w:Norman Davies|title=Vanished Kingdoms|page=202|publisher=Penguin|year_published=2012 |passage=The three '''estates''' of feudal lords, clergy and royal officers met in separate chambers, and exercised an advisory role.}} # {{lb|en|legal}} The nature and extent of a person's [[interest]] in, or [[ownership]] of, land. {{defdate|from 15th c.}} # An (especially extensive) area of [[land]], under a single ownership. {{defdate|from 18th c.}} #* {{RQ:Telegraph|title=Doddington's garden pyramid is a folly good show: The owners of a Lincolnshire stately home have brought the folly into the 21st century, by building a 30ft pyramid [print edition: Great pyramid of Lincolnshire, 6 September 2014, p. G2]|url=http://www.telegraph.co.uk/gardening/gardenstovisit/11074319/Doddingtons-garden-pyramid-is-a-folly-good-show.html|date=7 September 2014|passage=It has been a long time since new follies were springing up across the great '''estates''' of Britain. But the owners of Doddington Hall, in Lincolnshire, have brought the folly into the 21st century, by building a 30ft pyramid in the grounds of the Elizabethan manor.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250722234638/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/gardening/gardenstovisit/11074319/Doddingtons-garden-pyramid-is-a-folly-good-show.html|archivedate=22 July 2025}} # The landed property owned or controlled by a government or a department of government. # {{lb|en|UK|sometimes|_|pejorative}} A [[housing estate]]. {{defdate|from 20th c.}} #
